Web search results for query: "Angular router security advisory 2026 GHSA @angular/router"

Links: [{"title":"Security Advisories · angular/angular · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/angular/angular/security/advisories"},{"title":"Angular i18n vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting · CVE-2026-27970 · GitHub Advisory Database · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-prjf-86w9-mfqv"},{"title":"OSV - Open Source Vulnerabilities","url":"https://osv.dev/vulnerability/GHSA-ff3f-86qr-9cv3"},{"title":"Angular Server-Side Rendering (SSR): Denial of Service via Numeric URL Matrix Parameters · CVE-2026-101896 · GitHub Advisory Database · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-ff3f-86qr-9cv3"},{"title":"Security-Advisories: @angular/* auf 21.2.24 und axios auf 1.20.0 heben · Issue #451 · panary/panary-core","url":"https://github.com/panary/panary-core/issues/451"},{"title":"Angular Server-Side Rendering (SSR): Denial of Service via Numeric URL Matrix Parameters","url":"https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/@angular/router/CVE-2026-101896/"},{"title":"Security Alert","url":"https://github.com/AbsaOSS/StatusBoard/issues/68"},{"title":"Denial of Service via Numeric URL Matrix Parameters in Server-Side Rendering (SSR) · Advisory · angular/angular · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/angular/angular/security/advisories/GHSA-ff3f-86qr-9cv3"},{"title":"Hol","url":"https://hol.org/guard/security/cves/CVE-2026-101896-angular-server-side-rendering-ssr-denial-of"}]

The most relevant 2026 advisory for `@angular/router` I found is **GHSA-ff3f-86qr-9cv3**, a high-severity denial-of-service issue in server-side rendering (SSR), tracked as CVE-2026-101896. Its patched versions are 22.2.0, 21.2.24, and 20.3.32. It is rated 7.5 HIGH under CVSS 3.1 and classified under CWE-400 and CWE-770.

- **The flaw:** Numeric URL matrix parameters can make the V8 engine allocate oversized memory, so an unauthenticated attacker can crash a Node.js SSR worker with modest request volume. With 8 KB request paths, as few as 12–22 concurrent requests can crash a 256 MiB–512 MiB Node.js SSR worker.
- **Affected versions:** Affected are versions from 22.0.0 up to 22.2.0, from 21.0.0 up to 21.2.24, and from 20.0.0 up to 20.3.32, plus versions up to 19.2.25. The advisory says the older line has reached end of support and will not be patched.
- **Mitigations:** Until you upgrade, the advisory suggests blocking or stripping semicolons at a reverse proxy, limiting path depth, or raising the Node.js old-space limit.

Other SSR advisories on Angular's security page look router-related by title, but I did not confirm their affected package or versions:
- **GHSA-57xq-rjx2-v5xh** (published Oct 1, 2026, High): denial of service via RouterLink query parameter retention in SSR.
- **GHSA-62vg-58rm-qff7** (published Sep 30, 2026, High): denial of service via unmatched empty-path outlet route matching in SSR.
- **GHSA-w739-gvwx-grc3** (published Sep 30, 2026, Moderate): open redirect via protocol-relative URLs in SSR.

The Angular security page is the place to confirm these. The page's age metadata conflicts with its published dates, so I relied on the dates as written. The search also surfaced GHSA-prjf-86w9-mfqv (CVE-2026-27970), an XSS issue in the i18n pipeline. It affects `@angular/core`, not the router.

**Affected package:** `@angular/router` (npm)

| Affected range | Patched version |
|---|---|
| 22.0.0 to below 22.2.0 | 22.2.0 |
| 21.0.0 to below 21.2.24 | 21.2.24 |
| 20.0.0 to below 20.3.32 | 20.3.32 |
| 19.2.25 and earlier | None. The advisory states "End of Support / LTS expired; will not be patched" |

**SSR-only:** Yes. The issue occurs only when Server-Side Rendering runs on Node.js (V8) and `@angular/router` parses user-controlled request URLs. The advisory says pure client-side Angular apps are not vulnerable, because memory use in a user's browser doesn't cross a security boundary.

**Mitigations:**
- **Upgrade** to a patched version. This is the fix the advisory describes.
- **Reject or strip semicolons** at the reverse proxy or WAF so matrix parameters never reach the SSR service. The advisory gives an Nginx example that returns HTTP 400 for URIs containing `;`.
- **Limit path depth** by rejecting requests with an excessive number of segments (the advisory suggests roughly 20 to 30).
- **Raise `--max-old-space-size`** (e.g., to 2048 or 4096 MB). This only raises the load needed to crash the worker and does not fully eliminate the risk under sustained traffic.

content.text:
**Short answer:** You're on an affected version, but the bug can't be exploited in Financial HQ UI the way it's built. So this isn't urgent. Pick up the fix in your next routine dependency update.

**The advisory:** [GHSA-ff3f-86qr-9cv3](https://github.com/angular/angular/security/advisories/GHSA-ff3f-86qr-9cv3) (CVE-2026-101896), published Sep 23, 2026, rated High (7.5). Numbers placed after semicolons in a URL can make a Node.js server-side rendering (SSR) worker use too much memory and crash.
- Affected: `@angular/router` from 22.0.0 up to (but not including) 22.2.0, with matching ranges on the 21.x and 20.x lines.
- Fixed in: 22.2.0, 21.2.24 and 20.3.32.
- It only affects apps that render on the server. The advisory says apps that run purely in the browser are not vulnerable.

**Financial HQ UI:**
- `financial-hq-ui/package.json:56` pins `@angular/router` to `22.1.7`, and `yarn.lock` resolves to the same version. That is inside the affected range.
- The app doesn't render on the server. There's no `@angular/ssr`, `@angular/platform-server` or Express in its dependencies, and no SSR, server or prerender settings anywhere outside `yarn.lock`. It's a browser-only Nx workspace, so the vulnerable server code never runs.

The three other recent router-related advisories (GHSA-57xq-rjx2-v5xh, GHSA-62vg-58rm-qff7 and GHSA-w739-gvwx-grc3, all Sep 30–Oct 1) are also server-side only, so the same reasoning applies. I didn't check their exact affected versions.

**Recommendation:** Upgrade to 22.2.x in your normal update cycle. It closes the issue and stops security scanners from flagging it.
- Bump every `@angular/*` package together, because they're all pinned to `22.1.7` (the CLI and devkit packages are at `22.1.8`).
- Run the `postinstall` patch scripts and the tests afterwards, since those scripts patch third-party packages for Angular compatibility.

If anyone later adds server-side rendering to this app, or to another app that uses these packages, treat this as urgent and upgrade first.

Sources:
- [GHSA-ff3f-86qr-9cv3 – Angular advisory](https://github.com/angular/angular/security/advisories/GHSA-ff3f-86qr-9cv3)
- [Angular security advisories list](https://github.com/angular/angular/security/advisories)
- [GitHub Advisory Database entry](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-ff3f-86qr-9cv3)
- [GitLab advisory for @angular/router](https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/@angular/router/CVE-2026-101896/)
